item.title: K8s Up & Running.03 Deploying a Kubernetes Cluster
item.description: Four ways to get a cluster and what each hides — managed cloud in two commands, minikube’s single node, kind’s containers-as-nodes, kubeadm with every slot empty — then reading the cluster with kubectl: kubeconfig, version skew, node conditions, requests vs limits, and why kube-proxy is a DaemonSet while CoreDNS is a Deployment. Closes with the EKS auth path that explains why an EKS kubeconfig holds no key.
